original_question: Let A subseteq F2^n. If one must remove epsilon * 2^n elements from A to make it triangle-free, meaning there do not exist x, y, x+y in A, must the probability over uniform independent x,y in F2^n satisfy Pr[x,y,x+y in A] >= poly(epsilon)?
target_in_paper: The exact target is the open problem entry "Triangle Removal in F_2^n" in the main matter of arXiv:1204.6447 (pp. 5-6). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper on the ambient space F_2^n, the object A ⊆ F_2^n, the deletion-distance premise (needing ε·2^n deletions to become triangle-free), the meaning of triangle-freeness via x, y, x+y ∈ A, and the desired polynomial lower bound on the triangle density Pr[x,y,x+y ∈ A]. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447.pdf))
missing_details: State the universal quantifiers explicitly: for every n, every ε > 0, and every A ⊆ F_2^n satisfying the premise.
Clarify that "must remove ε·2^n elements" means at least ε·2^n elements must be deleted, not exactly that many.
Specify that x and y are chosen independently and uniformly from F_2^n; the paper states this explicitly.
Make explicit that no distinctness condition is imposed on x and y in the paper’s formulation.
Define "poly(ε)" in stand-alone form, e.g. c·ε^C for absolute constants c,C > 0.
Clarify that the lower bound is intended to depend only on ε, not on n or on the particular set A.
refined_question: Does there exist an absolute polynomial p(ε) = c·ε^C with c,C > 0 such that for every n, every ε > 0, and every subset A ⊆ F_2^n for which one must delete at least ε·2^n elements to obtain a triangle-free set (that is, a set containing no x,y ∈ F_2^n with x, y, and x+y all in the set), the ordered triangle density satisfies Pr[x ∈ A, y ∈ A, x+y ∈ A] ≥ p(ε), where x and y are chosen independently and uniformly from F_2^n?
justification: This is the closest official formulation in the paper: the entry titled "Triangle Removal in F_2^n" asks exactly whether an ε-far-from-triangle-free subset A ⊆ F_2^n must have triangle probability at least poly(ε). The nearby remarks only record the then-best known lower bound of Green and the upper-bound example of Bhattacharyya and Xie, so the faithful rewrite should stay with this one-set F_2^n formulation and simply make its quantifiers and the meaning of poly(ε) explicit. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6447.pdf))
